tb-E301-1.question:
The energy conversions of an electric fan are shown below (Fig a).

What is the end-use energy efficiency of the fan?

A E3E1×100%

B E2+E3E1×100%

C E3E1+E2×100%

D E1−E3E1×100%
tb-E301-1.reasoning:
End-use efficiency=useful output energy/input energy×100%. The fan's purpose is to move air, so useful output is the air's kinetic energy E₃ and input is electrical energy E₁.

Energy stored in the blades is not the final energy delivered to the air, and motor heating is a loss. The efficiency is E₃/E₁×100%: A.

tb-E301-2.question:
Which of the following statements about the cooling capacity of an air conditioner is/are correct?

(1) It is the rate at which heat is released to the outside by the air conditioner.

(2) Its unit is kW h.

(3) Its value can be larger than the power input of the air conditioner.

A (1) only

B (3) only

C (1) and (2) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-E301-2.reasoning:
Cooling capacity is the highest rate at which heat is removed from a room. The heat released to the outside includes the heat removed from the room and the work done by the air conditioner.

∴ (1) is incorrect.

tb-E301-4.question:
What happens to the refrigerant when it flows through the compressor in an air conditioner?

(1) Its volume decreases.

(2) Its pressure increases.

(3) Its temperature increases.

A (1) and (2) only

B (1) and (3) only

C (2) and (3) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-E301-4.reasoning:
The compressor does work on the refrigerant, increasing its pressure and temperature. Statements (2) and (3) hold, and the supplied answer is C.

The fixed volume of a pipe is different from the volume occupied by a fixed mass of refrigerant. If (1) means the latter, compression reduces that volume and all three statements give D. The question does not distinguish these meanings; C must not be taken to mean unchanged specific volume during compression.

tb-E301-5.question:
What happens to the refrigerant when it flows through the evaporator coil in an air conditioner?

(1) Its internal energy increases.

(2) Its volume increases.

(3) It absorbs energy from the room.

A (1) and (2) only

B (1) and (3) only

C (2) and (3) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-E301-5.reasoning:
In the evaporator, refrigerant absorbs energy from the room and vaporizes, increasing its internal energy and cooling the room. Statements (1) and (3) hold; the supplied answer is B.

For a fixed mass changing from liquid to gas, occupied volume normally increases, making (2) true as well and giving D. A fixed coil volume is not the same as unchanged specific volume of the refrigerant. The wording is ambiguous.

tb-E301-6.question:
Which of the following descriptions about different electric cookers is/are correct?

(1) In using an electric hotplate, heat is transferred from the coil of resistance wire to the cooking pot.

(2) In using an induction cooker, heat is transferred from the cooking pot to the top plate.

(3) In using a microwave oven, heat is transferred from the inner case of the oven to the food.

A (1) only

B (1) and (2) only

C (1) and (3) only

D (2) and (3) only
tb-E301-6.reasoning:
In a hotplate, the resistance wire heats electrically and transfers heat to the pot, so (1) is correct. An induction cooker heats the pot through induced currents; the hot pot can then warm the top plate, so (2) is correct.

A microwave oven primarily heats food by absorption of microwave energy, not by first heating the inner casing. Thus (3) is false: B.

tb-E301-9.question:
Two electric kettles have the same power output. They are used to boil the same amount of water from the same temperature. Which of the following statements is incorrect?

A The one with lower power input consumes less electricity.

B The one with higher end-use energy efficiency boils the water faster.

C The one with lower end-use energy efficiency consumes more electricity.

D The one with lower end-use energy efficiency loses more heat to the surrounding.
tb-E301-9.reasoning:
Heating equal masses of water through the same temperature rise requires the same useful energy Q=mcΔT. Equal useful output powers give equal times t=Q/Pₒᵤₜ, so greater efficiency does not make boiling faster here. B is incorrect.

Since η=Pₒᵤₜ/Pᵢₙ, higher efficiency at fixed output means lower input power. With the same heating time, Eᵢₙ=Pᵢₙt is larger for the less efficient kettle, as is wasted energy.

Appliances are graded in EELS by calculating their energy efficiency index Iε.

Iε=EacEav×100%

The grading scheme for electric storage water heaters is shown in Table a.

A 105 − 75105×100% = 28.6%

C 120 − 75120×100% = 37.5%

D 120 − 90120×100% = 25%
tb-E301-10.reasoning:

tb-E301-15.question:
Vivian uses an induction cooker to have a hotpot dinner (Fig d).

(a) Describe how the electrical energy supplied to the induction cooker becomes the internal energy of the food. (3 marks)

(b) The top plate of an induction cooker gets hot after using it for a hotpot dinner. Explain why. (1 mark)

(c) In the hotpot dinner, the induction cooker operates at 1200 W in average for 2 hours. The cost of electricity is $1.1 per kW h. Find the cost of electricity for the cooker. (2 marks)
tb-E301-15.answer:
(a) The a.c. in the coil produces a fast-changing magnetic field. The electrical energy converts to the energy in magnetic field. 1A

Eddy currents are then induced in the pot, so the energy in the magnetic field converts to the electrical energy of eddy currents in the pot. 1A

The electrical energy converts to the internal energy of the pot as the pot is heated up. By conduction, the internal energy of the pot converts to the internal energy of food. 1A

(b) Heat is transferred from the hot pot to the top plate by conduction. 1A

(c) Cost of electricity

= $1.1 × 1.2 × 2 1M

= $2.64 1A

tb-E301-16.question:
A bowl of soup is heated by a microwave oven.

(a) Describe how the soup is heated up by microwaves. (2 marks)

(b) A conventional oven emits infra-red radiation to heat up food. Explain why the middle of the soup gets hot more quickly when using a microwave oven than a conventional oven. (1 mark)

(c) The container should not be closed tightly when reheating the soup using a microwave oven (Fig e). Explain. (2 marks)
tb-E301-16.answer:
(a) The soup contains polar water molecules. The oscillating electric field of microwaves makes the water molecules flip rapidly. 1A

As they flip, they collide with other molecules, causing the average kinetic energy of the soup molecules to increase. 1A

Therefore, the temperature of the soup increases.

(b) Since the microwave can penetrate deeply into the food, the interior and the surface of the food can be heated up at the same time. 1A

Therefore, the middle of the soup gets hot more quickly when using a microwave oven.

(c) When the soup is heated up, steam is generated inside the container and a pressure is built up. 1A

The containers can explode. 1A
